Using
Lemma <REF_0001>
and the work done in the earlier sections of this chapter it is easy
to make a list of types of morphisms which are <ACCENT_0001>tale local on the
source-and-target. In each case we list the lemma which implies
the property is <ACCENT_0002>tale local on the source and the lemma which implies
the property is <ACCENT_0003>tale local on the target. In each case the third assumption
of
Lemma <REF_0002>
is trivial to check, and we omit it. Here is the list:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> flat, see
Lemmas <REF_0003> and
<REF_0004>,
<STRUCT_0003> locally of finite presentation, see
Lemmas <REF_0005> and
<REF_0006>,
<STRUCT_0004> locally finite type, see
Lemmas <REF_0007> and
<REF_0008>,
<STRUCT_0005> universally open, see
Lemmas <REF_0009> and
<REF_0010>,
<STRUCT_0006> syntomic, see
Lemmas <REF_0011> and
<REF_0012>,
<STRUCT_0007> smooth, see
Lemmas <REF_0013> and
<REF_0014>,
<STRUCT_0008> <ACCENT_0004>tale, see
Lemmas <REF_0015> and
<REF_0016>,
<STRUCT_0009> locally quasi-finite, see
Lemmas <REF_0017> and
<REF_0018>,
<STRUCT_0010> unramified, see
Lemmas <REF_0019> and
<REF_0020>,
<STRUCT_0011> G-unramified, see
Lemmas <REF_0021> and
<REF_0022>, and
<STRUCT_0012> add more here as needed.
<STRUCT_0013>
